title: Rectangular matrix operations
instructions:
Implement the small `Matrix` class in `matrix.py`.

## Files
- `matrix.py`

API:
- `Matrix(rows: list[list[int | float]])` accepts a nonempty rectangular
  list with at least one column. Empty outer lists, empty rows, or unequal
  row lengths raise `ValueError`. Copy the input rows so later caller
  mutations cannot change the matrix. Elements are guaranteed int or float.
- Read-only `shape: tuple[int, int]` is `(number_of_rows, number_of_columns)`.
- `to_list() -> list[list[int | float]]` returns independent copies of the
  outer list and every row.
- `add(other: Matrix) -> Matrix` returns elementwise addition. Both shapes
  must match; otherwise raise `ValueError`.
- `multiply(other: Matrix) -> Matrix` returns ordinary matrix multiplication:
  output `[i][j]` is `sum(self[i][k] * other[k][j])`. The left column count
  must equal the right row count; otherwise raise `ValueError`.
- `transpose() -> Matrix` returns the matrix whose rows are the original
  columns, including for one-row and one-column matrices.

Every operation returns a new Matrix and leaves both inputs unchanged.
Support negative numbers, zero, rectangular shapes, and floats. No operator
overloads or validation of unsupported argument types is required.
